text: pharmr.extra R package extends pharmr — R bindings Python’s Pharmpy PK modeling library — higher-level utilities bug workarounds. Core layer: Functions call Python via reticulate (virtualenv ~/.virtualenvs/r-reticulate). pharmr package handles base Python bindings; package adds orchestration top. Two model backends: NONMEM (via Pharmpy) nlmixr2 (pure R). Key entry points: - create_model() — Builds Pharmpy model object (main heavy function R/create_model.R) - run_nlme() — Fits model (preferred deprecated fit_model()) - run_sim() / run_simulation() — Simulation utilities Pharmpy API compatibility: Several functions handle differences pharmpy v1.x v2.0+ (e.g., set_dv.R uses ColumnInfo type detection). touching dataset/datainfo manipulation, check API paths. Known bug workarounds: R/read_modelfit_results.R overrides pharmr::read_modelfit_results() fixes SAEM+IMP multi-step estimation failures. See memory file details four bugs patched .

title: SIR covariance estimation in NONMEM
text: Sampling Importance Resampling (SIR) method estimating parameter uncertainty NONMEM (7.3+) can run part $COVARIANCE step. works : Sampling parameter vectors proposal distribution (typically asymptotic normal distribution centered FOCE estimates, covariance matrix variance). Weighting sample well matches observed data relative proposal distribution. Resampling replacement according weights, yielding set parameter draws approximate true posterior. output set weighted parameter vectors rather single covariance matrix, makes SIR robust standard covariance step : dataset small asymptotic covariance matrix unreliable. model highly nonlinear parameter distributions skewed. standard covariance step fails (e.g., non-positive-definite R matrix). full multivariate uncertainty distribution needed simulation. SIR slower standard covariance step much faster nonparametric bootstrap, produces uncertainty estimates closely match likelihood profiling practice (Dosne et al., 2016, doi:10.1007/s10928-016-9487-8).

title: SIR covariance estimation in NONMEM
text: Three plots lst-file output help assess SIR quality: dOFV distribution — distribution dOFV = OFV(sample) - OFV(FOCE) values SIR samples follow chi-squared distribution. distribution shifted right, proposal narrow; increase SIRSAMPLE. Spatial trends — scatter plot importance ratios vs. individual parameters. flat (horizontal) trend indicates good proposal match. bell-shaped trend means proposal wide; U-shaped trend means narrow. Temporal trends — importance ratio vs. sample index. flat trend indicates good samples depleted. trend drifts iterations, increase SIRSAMPLE SIRNITER.
